summary: This program stores a playlist in a Queue so songs are played strictly in the order they were added, then drains the queue one song at a time. It shows the three core queue operations: offer to add at the back, peek to look at the front, and poll to remove from the front.

lines.text: The variable is typed as Queue but built from a LinkedList, so the code can only use the queue's first-in, first-out operations even though the underlying object could do more. This is what keeps a song from jumping the line.
The offer method tries to add the song to the back of the queue and returns false if it cannot, rather than throwing an exception the way add would.
Peeking reports which song is up next without removing it, exactly like a streaming service showing the next episode before it plays.
Each call to poll removes and returns the song at the front of the queue, which is why the loop condition eventually becomes false and the drain terminates.

lines.code: System.out.println("Queue after processing all songs: " + songQueue);
lines.text: Because polling removes items as it processes them, the queue is empty at the end and prints as an empty pair of brackets.
